topics.topic_name: Smart City Pillars, ICT Pipeline & Data Fusion
topics.description: Smart city pillars, data gathering/processing pipeline, and multi-sensor fusion.

questions.question: What is a Smart City?

options.A: An urban area using ICT and IoT technology to optimize municipal operational efficiency, governance, and resource management
options.D: A paper model of a town

questions.justification: Smart Cities leverage ICT and connected sensors to address urban density, transport, health, and resource management.

questions.question: What are the core operational pillars of a Smart City framework?

options.A: Smart Economy, Smart Governance, Smart Mobility, Smart Environment, Smart Living, and Smart Health

questions.justification: Smart city frameworks encompass economy, governance, mobility, environment, living, and health.

questions.question: What is the primary technological pipeline supporting Smart City operations?

options.A: Data Gathering -> Transmission -> Storage -> Processing / Analytics

questions.justification: The smart city technological pipeline collects sensor data, transmits it across networks, stores it, and extracts operational insights.

questions.question: According to Week 10 Assignment Question 4, what refers to combining information from multiple sensor sources?

options.A: Multi-sensor data fusion

questions.justification: Multi-sensor data fusion synthesizes readings from multiple heterogeneous sensors to improve situational accuracy.

questions.question: According to Week 10 Assignment Question 3, what are the primary characteristics of Smart Health systems?

options.A: Low-cost/portable, supports remote check-ups & diagnosis, and enables effortless continuous monitoring

questions.justification: Smart health provides portable, continuous, low-cost remote monitoring and diagnosis.

questions.question: What major implementation challenges face urban-scale IoT deployments in Smart Cities (Week 10 slides)?

options.A: Heterogeneity of hardware/software, scalability across millions of devices, security vulnerabilities, and privacy concerns
options.B: Lack of physical ground space for sensors

questions.justification: Urban IoT faces heterogeneity, massive scale, cybersecurity threats, and user data privacy concerns.

questions.question: How does Energy Harvesting enhance sensor longevity in Smart City municipal monitoring?

options.A: Dedicated circuits harvest ambient solar, thermal, or vibrational energy near IoT nodes to supplement battery power
options.B: By replacing batteries with diesel fuel
options.D: By running high-voltage AC lines to every sensor

questions.justification: Energy harvesting captures ambient environmental energy (solar, vibration, thermal) to extend node lifespan.

questions.question: In urban energy harvesting, what factors determine the amount of energy successfully harvested by an IoT node?

options.A: Sensitivity of the harvesting circuit, distance between device and energy source, and ambient environmental conditions

questions.justification: Harvested energy yields depend on circuit sensitivity, source distance, and ambient source strength.

questions.question: Why is Communication Medium Selection crucial in Smart City sensor network planning?

options.A: Different urban sensing tasks require tailored tradeoffs between data rate, radio range, penetration through structures, and power consumption
options.B: All sensors must use satellite links
options.C: Copper wires are mandatory for mobile vehicles

questions.justification: Urban environments demand diverse communication technologies (NB-IoT, LoRaWAN, Wi-Fi, 5G) based on specific application range and bandwidth requirements.

questions.question: How does multi-sensor data fusion improve incident detection (e.g. fire or traffic collision) in smart cities?

options.A: By cross-correlating evidence from optical cameras, acoustic sensors, and thermal detectors to dramatically reduce false alarms

questions.justification: Data fusion synthesizes redundant and complementary sensor data streams, confirming incidents reliably.

topics.topic_name: Smart Home Systems & Intelligent Energy Management
topics.description: Smart home infrastructure, HEMS, demand response, and net metering.

questions.question: What constitutes a Smart Home infrastructure?

options.A: Intelligent networking devices and seamless integration of appliances using wired/wireless communication for automated control
options.C: A home powered entirely by gas lamps

questions.justification: Smart homes combine connected appliances, sensors, and intelligent control controllers.

questions.question: What is a primary objective of Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) in smart homes?

options.A: To optimize energy usage and shift heavy appliance operation from on-peak to off-peak hours
options.C: To cut off power during night

questions.justification: HEMS schedules smart appliances during off-peak rate hours to minimize electricity costs.

questions.question: Which protocol standards enable wireless device communication inside smart homes?

options.A: ZigBee, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and BLE

questions.justification: Smart home devices commonly utilize ZigBee, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth Low Energy.

questions.question: True or False: Computerized controls in smart homes help minimize grid stress during peak demand hours.

options.A: True

questions.justification: Smart home controls automatically reduce or shift power consumption during grid peak load intervals.

questions.question: Which device acts as the central local hub coordinating smart home sensors, actuators, and cloud control apps?

options.A: Smart Home Gateway / Hub

questions.justification: The Smart Home Gateway acts as the central hub bridging local home sensors to user apps.

questions.question: How do Demand Response (DR) signals sent from utility operators interact with Smart Home controllers?

options.A: Utility DR signals notify the home controller of high grid load/pricing, prompting HEMS to automatically dim lights or delay HVAC cycles
options.B: DR signals physically blow home fuses
options.D: DR signals format the user's phone

questions.justification: Demand Response protocols allow utilities to send real-time pricing or load reduction requests to automated HEMS controllers.

questions.question: Why is privacy protection a major challenge in Smart Home IoT implementations?

options.A: Detailed smart meter and occupancy sensor logs can reveal precise daily resident habits, presence, and personal activities
options.B: Smart home devices transmit no data
options.D: Privacy is protected by physics automatically

questions.justification: Granular high-frequency sensor readings (energy, motion, presence) can expose resident routines if unencrypted.

questions.question: In a smart home, how does an automated HVAC system interact with occupancy and window status sensors?

options.A: If window sensors report OPEN, the HEMS pauses HVAC operation to prevent wasted energy
options.B: The HVAC increases heat to maximum when windows open
options.D: The sensor reboots the home network

questions.justification: Cross-sensor automation prevents energy waste by pausing climate control when perimeter openings are detected.

questions.question: What security mechanism prevents unauthorized hackers from controlling smart home locks or surveillance cameras?

options.A: End-to-end encryption, strong mutual authentication, secure firmware boot, and regular patch management

questions.justification: Robust authentication, encrypted data channels, and secure boot prevent unauthorized access to home actuators.

questions.question: How does Net Metering benefit smart home owners equipped with rooftop solar PV panels?

options.A: It allows homeowners to sell excess generated solar power back to the grid, receiving credits against their electricity bill
options.B: It taxes solar panel owners extra
options.C: It stores power in cloud databases
options.D: It disconnects the house from grid

questions.justification: Net metering measures bidirectional power flow, crediting consumers for surplus renewable energy supplied to the grid.

topics.description: V2X paradigms, OBUs/RSUs, IEEE 802.11p DSRC, and in-vehicle networks.

questions.question: What is the Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) paradigm in Intelligent Transportation Systems?

options.A: A vehicular communication framework enabling wireless information sharing between vehicles, infrastructure, pedestrians, and network clouds

questions.justification: V2X enables vehicles to communicate wirelessly with other vehicles (V2V), infrastructure (V2I), pedestrians (V2P), and networks (V2N).

questions.question: According to Week 9 Assignment Question 10, what network architecture property characterizes V2X communications?

options.A: Distributed architecture where content is widely distributed over the network
options.B: Restricted to a single centralized source

questions.justification: V2X relies on a distributed architecture where information is disseminated across mobile nodes and RSUs.

questions.question: Which unit installed inside a connected vehicle hosts sensors and onboard wireless communication devices?

options.A: OBU (On-Board Unit)

questions.justification: On-Board Units (OBUs) are installed in vehicles for processing and V2X communication.

questions.question: Which static unit deployed along highways interfaces with passing connected vehicles?

options.A: RSU (Road-Side Unit)

questions.justification: Road-Side Units (RSUs) are stationary roadside infrastructure nodes that communicate with vehicle OBUs.

questions.question: Which protocol stack standard is dedicated to Short-Range Vehicular Communication (DSRC) in the Ad-hoc Domain?

options.A: IEEE 802.11p / WAVE

questions.justification: DSRC (Dedicated Short-Range Communications) utilizes IEEE 802.11p for vehicular wireless access.

questions.question: In the In-Vehicle Domain, which communication networks connect Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) sensors, radar, and cameras?

options.A: CAN (Controller Area Network), VPLN (Vehicular Powerline Network), and Automotive Ethernet

questions.justification: In-vehicle systems communicate internally over CAN bus, VPLN, and Ethernet.

questions.question: What are the primary operational goals of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) safety messages (e.g. Emergency Electronic Brake Light)?

options.A: To broadcast collision warning alerts within milliseconds, preventing multi-vehicle pileups during sudden deceleration

questions.justification: V2V safety messages deliver low-latency hazard alerts to neighboring vehicles to avoid crashes.

questions.question: What major challenges impede widespread V2X deployment in smart cities?

options.A: High vehicle mobility causing rapid network topology shifts, severe privacy/location tracking risks, security against rogue message injection, and lack of unified global standards

questions.justification: V2X faces extreme mobility, strict low-latency requirements, location privacy risks, and cybersecurity threats.

questions.question: How does Vehicular Cloud Computing assist connected vehicles during urban traffic congestion?

options.A: By offloading heavy traffic image processing and route optimization computations from OBUs to edge vehicular clouds or RSUs

questions.justification: Vehicular cloud computing pools nearby vehicular and edge resources to execute real-time traffic and route computations.

questions.question: What is Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) power flow in smart grid connected electric vehicles?

options.A: EVs discharge excess battery power back into the smart power grid during peak demand, acting as distributed energy storage
options.B: EVs consume grid power without limit
options.D: EVs run on solar energy exclusively

questions.justification: V2G allows electric vehicles to export stored battery energy back to the grid during peak demand hours.
